```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse   = TRUE,
  comment    = "#>",
  fig.align  = "center",
  fig.width  = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  out.width  = "80%",
  dpi        = 150,
  message    = FALSE,

)

# This template knits before you replace any placeholder: every paper-specific
# chunk is `eval = FALSE` until you edit it.
#
# Save the file under inst/replications/<NN>_<Topic>/ with a short bibkey-style
# name such as thornton2008demand.Rmd: R limits package paths to 100 bytes.
#
# Estimators, tables, and plots are called directly from their packages.
# causalmetrics supplies est_aipw() and the LaTeX wrappers table_task(),
# wrap_latex_table(), plot_task(), and wrap_latex_figure().
required_pkgs <- c(
  "causalmetrics", "haven", "dplyr", "tidyr", "broom", "estimatr", "fixest",
  "modelsummary", "kableExtra", "ggplot2"
)
missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[
  !vapply(required_pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  message(
    "Install before running the empirical chunks: ",
    paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
if (requireNamespace("causalmetrics", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(causalmetrics))
}

options(modelsummary_factory_latex = "kableExtra")
options(modelsummary_factory_html  = "kableExtra")

# Helpers local to this replication. They are not package exports.
fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f", big.mark = ","))
}
```

# Pedagogical goal {.unnumbered}

> **One sentence: what should a reader learn from this replication?**
>
> Example: *How to move from a randomized encouragement design to an IV
> analysis when take-up is endogenous, while auditing sample construction,
> attrition, balance, and first-stage strength.*

This replication uses **[Author (Year)]** to illustrate **[identification
strategy]**. The paper asks [one-sentence research question]. The point is to
teach the workflow for this design, not to reproduce every table in the paper.

**Not replicated here:**

- [Robustness check]: [reason for exclusion]
- [Supplementary specification]: [reason]

# Research question

- **Question.** [What causal effect, of what treatment, on which outcome, for whom?]
- **Mechanism.** [Why the treatment should move the outcome, in the paper's own theory.]
- **Why this design.** [Why this identification strategy fits the setting; what the naive comparison gets wrong.]

# Design and identification

- **Estimand.** [ATE / ATT / ITT / LATE / CATE], defined for [population].
- **Assumptions.** [Formal statement, then the plain-English version.]
- **Threats.** [What could break identification and how the paper addresses each threat.]
- **Estimator.** [Be specific. Example: "TWFE is inappropriate under staggered adoption; the paper uses Sun-Abraham via `fixest::sunab()`."]

| Role | Variable | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| Unit | `unit_var` | [description] |
| Time | `time_var` | [description] |
| Assignment $Z$ | `assign_var` | [description; equals $D$ under perfect compliance] |
| Treatment $D$ | `treat_var` | [description] |
| Outcome $Y$ | `outcome_var` | [description] |
| Controls | `cov1`, `cov2` | pre-treatment only |
| Cluster | `cluster_var` | [level of assignment or of correlated shocks] |

# Data and sample construction

> **What this section teaches:** sample restrictions change the estimand, so
> record them before estimating anything.

```{r load-data, eval = FALSE}
if (!file.exists(params$data_path)) {
  stop(
    "Data file not found: ", params$data_path,
    "\nUpdate params$data_path in the YAML header."
  )
}
raw <- haven::read_dta(params$data_path)

# Paper-specific cleaning and variable construction stay in this file.
dt <- raw |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # treat_var   = ...,
    # outcome_var = ...
  )
```

```{r sample-flow, eval = FALSE}
# Record observation counts at each restriction. Edit the steps.
steps <- list(
  "Raw file"             = function(d) d,
  "Drop missing outcome" = function(d) dplyr::filter(d, !is.na(outcome_var)),
  "Analysis sample"      = function(d) dplyr::filter(d, sample_flag == 1)
)
flow <- Reduce(
  function(acc, nm) {
    d <- steps[[nm]](acc$data)
    acc$table <- rbind(acc$table, data.frame(Step = nm, Observations = nrow(d)))
    acc$data <- d
    acc
  },
  names(steps),
  init = list(data = dt, table = NULL)
)
analysis_sample <- flow$data

flow$table |>
  table_task(format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) |>
  wrap_latex_table(
    caption = "Sample construction.",
    label   = "tab:sample_flow",
    notes   = "Observation counts after each restriction."
  )
```

# Descriptive statistics

> **What this section teaches:** [one idea, e.g. why raw group differences
> motivate the design]

```{r summary-stats, eval = FALSE}
modelsummary::datasummary_balance(
  ~ treat_var,
  data   = dplyr::select(analysis_sample, treat_var, cov1, cov2, outcome_var),
  output = "kableExtra"
) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "HOLD_position") |>
  wrap_latex_table(
    caption = "Summary statistics by treatment status.",
    label   = "tab:summary"
  )
```

# Design-specific diagnostics

> **What this section teaches:** what to check before estimation for this
> identification strategy.

Keep the diagnostics that match the design and delete the rest.

**Randomized assignment or encouragement.** Assignment rate by arm, baseline
balance with robust standard errors, attrition by arm, and take-up when $Z$
differs from $D$.

```{r rct-diagnostics, eval = FALSE}
analysis_sample |>
  dplyr::count(assign_var) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = n / sum(n))

balance <- lapply(c("cov1", "cov2"), function(v) {
  fit <- estimatr::lm_robust(
    stats::reformulate("assign_var", response = v),
    data    = analysis_sample,
    se_type = "HC2"
  )
  data.frame(
    covariate  = v,
    difference = fit$coefficients[["assign_var"]],
    std_error  = fit$std.error[["assign_var"]]
  )
})
do.call(rbind, balance) |>
  table_task(digits = 3) |>
  wrap_latex_table(caption = "Baseline balance.", label = "tab:balance")
```

**Selection on observables.** Propensity-score overlap, weight tails,
effective sample size, and balance after weighting or matching.
`est_aipw()` reports the first three in its `$diagnostics`.

```{r soo-diagnostics, eval = FALSE}
ps_fit <- glm(treat_var ~ cov1 + cov2, data = analysis_sample, family = binomial())
analysis_sample$p_hat <- predict(ps_fit, type = "response")

plot_task(analysis_sample, ggplot2::aes(x = p_hat, fill = factor(treat_var))) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(
    ggplot2::aes(y = ggplot2::after_stat(density)),
    bins = 30, alpha = 0.5, position = "identity"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Estimated propensity score", y = "Density", fill = "Treated")
```

**Instrumental variables.** First-stage strength and the reduced form,
clustered at the level of assignment.

```{r iv-diagnostics, eval = FALSE}
first_stage <- fixest::feols(
  treat_var ~ instrument_var + cov1 | fe_var,
  data    = analysis_sample,
  cluster = ~ cluster_var
)
summary(first_stage)
```

**Difference-in-differences.** Treatment timing by cohort, pre-trends, and
the choice between TWFE and a heterogeneity-robust estimator.

```{r did-diagnostics, eval = FALSE}
timing <- analysis_sample |>
  dplyr::group_by(unit_var) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cohort = suppressWarnings(min(time_var[treat_var == 1])),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

plot_task(timing, ggplot2::aes(x = cohort)) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "First treated period", y = "Units")
```

**Regression discontinuity.** Density (manipulation) test, covariate
continuity at the cutoff, and bandwidth sensitivity with `rdrobust` and
`rddensity`.

# Estimation

> **What this section teaches:** the main estimator for this design, called
> directly from its package.

```{r estimate, eval = FALSE}
# Keep the block that matches the design; delete the rest.

# Experiment or encouragement design: ITT with robust SEs, then LATE via IV.
fit_itt <- estimatr::lm_robust(
  outcome_var ~ assign_var + cov1,
  data     = analysis_sample,
  clusters = cluster_var
)
fit_late <- estimatr::iv_robust(
  outcome_var ~ treat_var + cov1 | assign_var + cov1,
  data     = analysis_sample,
  clusters = cluster_var
)

# Selection on observables: AIPW with cross-fitted nuisance predictions.
fit_aipw <- est_aipw(
  analysis_sample,
  y = "outcome_var", d = "treat_var", x = c("cov1", "cov2"),
  folds = 5, seed = 1
)

# Instrumental variables with fixed effects.
fit_iv <- fixest::feols(
  outcome_var ~ cov1 | fe_var | treat_var ~ instrument_var,
  data    = analysis_sample,
  cluster = ~ cluster_var
)
fixest::fitstat(fit_iv, ~ ivf1 + ivwald1)

# Staggered difference-in-differences via Sun-Abraham.
fit_did <- fixest::feols(
  outcome_var ~ fixest::sunab(cohort_var, time_var) | unit_var + time_var,
  data    = analysis_sample,
  cluster = ~ cluster_var
)
summary(fit_did, agg = "att")
```

## Regression table

```{r regtable, eval = FALSE}
modelsummary::modelsummary(
  list("ITT" = fit_itt, "LATE" = fit_late),
  output    = "kableExtra",
  estimate  = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  stars     = c("*" = 0.1, "**" = 0.05, "***" = 0.01),
  coef_map  = c("assign_var" = "Assigned", "treat_var" = "Treated"),
  gof_map   = c("nobs", "r.squared")
) |>
  wrap_latex_table(
    caption = "Main estimates.",
    label   = "tab:main",
    notes   = "Standard errors clustered at [level] in parentheses."
  )
```

## Figure

```{r main-figure, eval = FALSE}
coef_df <- broom::tidy(fit_itt, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)")

fig <- plot_task(coef_df, ggplot2::aes(x = term, y = estimate)) +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Estimate")

wrap_latex_figure(
  fig,
  caption = "Main estimates.",
  label   = "fig:main",
  notes   = "Bars are 95 percent confidence intervals."
)
```

# Interpretation

[2-4 paragraphs.]

- What the point estimate means substantively.
- Which population the estimand refers to (ATE, ATT, ITT, LATE) and why.
- Magnitude relative to the outcome's baseline level.
- Comparison with the paper's headline number.
- Limitations the paper acknowledges.
